📋 Real Logic for Interactive Tour Implementation
What I Want to Achieve:
A step-by-step guided tour that shows new users how to use the timetable app by:

Highlighting each section of the app one at a time
Darkening everything else so users focus on that specific section
Showing an explanation box directly underneath the highlighted section
Having a big "Next" button to move to the next step


🎯 The Flow:
Step 1: When User First Registers

After account creation, show a popup asking:

"Would you like a tour?"
Two buttons: "Yes (Recommended)" or "No Thanks"


If Yes → Start the tour immediately
If No → Show message: "You can find the tutorial in Settings anytime"
Save choice in storage so it doesn't ask again


Step 2: Tour Starts
For each feature in the app, do this sequence:
Visual Effect:

Entire screen goes dark (black transparent overlay ~75% opacity)
One specific section lights up (upload box, schedule view, etc.)
That section gets a glowing blue border/shadow to make it stand out
Everything else is dimmed and unclickable

Info Box Appears:

Directly below the highlighted section (not floating randomly)
Blue arrow pointing UP from the info box to the section
Info box contains:

Icon representing the feature
Title (e.g., "Upload Your Timetable")
Clear explanation of what this section does
Step indicator (e.g., "Step 1 of 8")
Progress dots showing where you are
BIG "Next" button (full width, blue, impossible to miss)
Small links for "← Previous" and "Skip Tutorial"




Step 3: The Tour Sequence
Go through these sections in order:

Upload Section - "Drag your timetable image here, AI will extract it"
Add Manually Button - "Or add classes yourself one by one"
Schedule View - "Your classes will appear here organized by day"
Study Together - "Create a session with a secret code, chat and study with friends"
AI Assistant - "Ask AI for help with homework anytime"
Notification Bell - "Get reminders before your classes"
Premium Card - "Unlock more features with monthly/yearly plans"
Settings Gear - "Customize everything and access this tutorial again"

Each time user clicks Next, move to the next section.

Step 4: Technical Requirements
What I Need to Track:

Current step number (0-7)
Tour active status (true/false)
Whether user completed tour (stored permanently)

How Highlighting Works:

Give each section an ID (like id="upload-section")
When that step is active, apply CSS that:

Makes that section z-index: 50 (on top)
Adds glowing blue shadow around it
Everything else is covered by dark overlay at z-index: 40



Info Box Position:

Use JavaScript to find the highlighted section's position on screen
Calculate where it ends (bottom edge)
Place info box 20-30px below that section
Center it horizontally
Add upward-pointing triangle/arrow above the box


Step 5: User Actions
Next Button:

Moves to next step
On last step, says "Finish Tour" instead
Saves completion status
Removes overlay and tour UI

Previous Button:

Goes back one step (disabled on step 1)

Skip Button:

Closes tour immediately
Saves "skipped" status
User can restart later from Settings

X Button:

Same as Skip


Step 6: After Tour Ends

Save to storage: tour_completed: true
Never show welcome popup again (check storage on login)
Add "Tutorial" option in Settings that calls the same tour function
Users can replay anytime


🎨 Visual Design Rules:

Dark overlay: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.75) covering everything
Highlighted section: Bright, with blue glow box-shadow: 0 0 60px rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.6)
Info box: White background, rounded corners, blue border
Next button: Blue gradient, large text, full width
Arrow: Blue triangle pointing up to section
Progress dots: Active = long blue bar, past = small blue dot, future = gray dot


💾 Storage Structure:
javascript// Save this when tour ends
{
  tour_completed: true,  // or false
  completed_date: 1234567890,
  skipped: false  // true if user skipped
}

🔄 Integration with Real App:
When you implement this in your actual timetable app:

Show welcome popup after successful registration
Match the section IDs with your real components
Position info boxes dynamically based on actual element positions
Make sure tour works on mobile (smaller boxes, adjusted positions)
Add "Tutorial" button in Settings that restarts the tour

Yes, **it is true**.

Google Cloud displays this warning because storing sensitive information (like API keys, database passwords, or private keys) in plain text Environment Variables is a security risk.

Here is why:

1.  **Visibility**: Anyone in your organization with "Viewer" permissions for that Google Cloud Project can go to the Cloud Run console and read your API Key in plain text. If you use Secret Manager, the value is hidden and encrypted.
2.  **Rotation & Updates**: If you need to change your API key (e.g., if it gets leaked), using Environment Variables requires you to **re-deploy** your entire service to update the value. 3.  **Audit Logging**: Secret Manager provides logs of exactly *who* accessed a secret and *when*, which is crucial for security auditing.

**Recommendation:**
While it is not "broken" to leave it as an environment variable for a prototype or hobby project, for a production application, you should ideally move the `API_KEY` to **Google Secret Manager** and mount it as an environment variable in Cloud Run.

### 1. Tracks Current Week's Progress
It visualizes your study habits for the current week (Monday to Sunday) using the data from your generated `smartPlan` (scheduled hours) and `trackedData` (actual completed sessions).
